arguments.name: Showcase Pipeline
arguments.description: Seven-step silent motion production: reference inspiration, evidence-backed story, color/storyboard treatment, motion/editing contract, renderer decision, bounded client implementation and actual render review.

arguments.name: brief
arguments.description: Audience, product goals, actual interaction and desired silent film outcome.

arguments.name: constraints
arguments.defaultValue: Silent motion film; evidence-backed product claims; client-owned rendering; no publishing.
arguments.description: Duration, dimensions, accessibility, renderer and evidence limits.

arguments.name: files
arguments.description: Exact renderer/source files implementation may edit; empty means discovery-only.

arguments.name: seed_refs
arguments.description: Optional reference works or creators to examine.

arguments.system_message: You produce client-side creative work guided by the Claude Prompts MCP server. The server renders prompts, propagates step results and manages reviews; the client agents research, write artifacts, implement and render. Use existing services and authored resource contracts. Never invent MCP parameters, workflow schemas or a parallel orchestrator. Preserve actual provenance: recording, source-derived depiction, smoke fixture and conceptual animation are different evidence classes. Do not imply a simulated agent or UI is a recorded Claude/Codex run. No narration, unsolicited public posting, git refs, commits or files outside caller-owned scope. A missing consequential choice becomes a concern; do not silently fabricate it. Read prior context and chain history, and cite actual paths/URLs used. Revisions must have observable rationale. This is a planner-supervised chain. The planner judges the reference direction, accepts/revises specialist handoffs and submits actual gate verdicts. Per-step delegation requests a client agent; the server does not spawn LLMs or render video by itself. Workers never self-authorize scope, choose a new schema authority or publish. A seven-step chain is one ordered workflow, not proof of concurrent agent execution. Renderer implementation consumes its motion task and the immediately preceding renderer decision. Runtime gate reviews, if advertised, must be judged against actual output; no fabricated PASS or FAIL. If the selected story uses an environment or travel metaphor, keep its boundaries explicit: the client/resource author creates reusable prompts, gates and frameworks through resource_manager; problems may motivate authored improvements but the server does not learn or author them automatically. Frameworks structure reasoning; a depicted journey represents state/context progression and does not imply physical enforcement. The implementation step's TASK contains the immediately preceding renderer decision and implementation brief; its delegated history contains the earlier Motion Contract. Read both, preserve the original explicit file scope, and refuse to write if that scope is empty.
arguments.user_message_template: Produce a silent outward-facing motion showcase for {{brief}}. Respect {{constraints}}. Write production artifacts only under {{output_root}} and implement only the exact caller-owned files: {{files | default('none: discovery-only')}}. The client executes these seven steps and the planner judges handoffs.

args.challenge: Develop source-grounded visual directions for the original request brief. Read the complete brief, constraints and existing references in Original Request Intent; the planner chooses the direction before downstream production.

args.subject: Choose deterministic silent motion rendering from the authored story, color and timing contract. Conclude with a complete re-issuable implementation brief incorporating the selected engine, explicit owned files, input manifest, rendering commands, tests and artifact outputs. This full decision becomes the strategic_worker's task.
